newsitem.title: Taiwan: Taiwan foreign minister in secret Malaysia trip - TV.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan foreign minister in secret Malaysia trip - TV.

text.p: Taiwan Foreign Minister John Chang flew to Malaysia on Friday, a day after he returned from a secretive trip to Indonesia, state television reported.
"John Chang's trip is very secretive. He uses an alias to avoid the media," Taiwan Television said.
The visit is sure to anger China, which views Taiwan as a renegade province not entitled to any international contacts.
Both Malaysia and Indonesia recognise China instead of Taiwan, which have been separated since their civil war in 1949.
The television report said Chang made a brief stopover in Singapore and arrived in Malaysia's capital of Kuala Lumpur in the afternoon.
"John Chang is expected to return to Taipei at 2300 local time tomorrow," the television said. It did not give sources for the information.
The foreign ministry declined to comment.
Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas has confirmed that he met with Chang in Jakarta on Wednesday, but stressed that he did so in an individual capacity.
China said on Friday it had made serious representations with Indonesia for hosting Chang.

Chang's trip to Indonesia followed Taiwan Vice-President Lien Chan's secret visit to the Ukraine last month. Beijing has accused the former Soviet republic of violating the "one China" commitment it made in establishing bilateral ties.
Only 30 countries, mostly in Africa and central America, recognise Taiwan's Republic of China government.
Taiwan says its 21 million people have a right to a voice in the United Nations and other forums. It has pushed to win new foreign friends and raise its international profile.
Taiwanese President Lee Teng-hui made an unofficial visit to Jakarta in February 1994. China, which has diplomatic ties with Indonesia, was enraged by the visit and protested to Jakarta.
